_review: TODO-REVIEW: All questions must be reviewed by a Lagos property lawyer before publication.
intro: These are suggested questions to ask your Lagos property lawyer or estate surveyor before proceeding. They are not exhaustive. A good professional will also raise matters you have not thought to ask.

questions.q: What is the nature of the title being offered — is it a Certificate of Occupancy, a registered Deed of Assignment, or something else?
questions.why: Different title types carry different levels of legal protection.

questions.q: Have you conducted an official search at the Lagos State Land Bureau, and what did it reveal?
questions.why: The search result is the most authoritative check on encumbrances and adverse interests.

questions.q: Is Governor's Consent in place for each transfer in the chain, including this one?
questions.why: Under the Land Use Act 1978, any alienation without Governor's Consent is void.

questions.q: Who is the registered owner, and have you confirmed the seller's identity against that registration?
questions.why: Impersonation of a true owner is a common fraud type.

questions.q: Are there any court orders, caveats, or injunctions affecting this property?
questions.why: Active litigation can freeze the property or reverse a completed purchase.

questions.q: Does the land fall within any government acquisition scheme, road alignment, or public infrastructure corridor?
questions.why: Such land cannot be privately developed and the government may enter at any time.

questions.q: What are my total costs beyond the purchase price, including stamp duty, registration, and your professional fees?
questions.why: Government fees and professional costs can add substantially to the headline price.

questions.q: What conditions precedent must be satisfied before I release final payment?
questions.why: Releasing payment before conditions are met leaves you with limited recourse.

questions.q: How long will it take to obtain Governor's Consent, and who is responsible for making the application?
questions.why: Governor's Consent can take months. Clarity on responsibility avoids delay or blame disputes.

questions.q: What are my remedies if the seller fails to deliver a perfected title after I have paid?
questions.why: Understanding your remedies before signing is better than discovering them in a courtroom.

questions.q: Are you registered with the Surveyors Registration Council of Nigeria (SURCON)?
questions.why: Only SURCON-registered surveyors may lawfully prepare survey plans in Nigeria.

questions.q: Does the survey plan on file at the Lagos State Survey Office match the parcel I am being shown?
questions.why: Sellers sometimes show one parcel and present documents for another.

questions.q: Does the land fall within any global acquisition area, committed government scheme, or buffer zone?
questions.why: Land within such areas cannot be privately owned or developed.

questions.q: What are the actual coordinates and dimensions of the parcel, and do they match what is stated in the title document?
questions.why: A discrepancy between the title and the survey may indicate a documentation error or fraud.

questions.q: Are there any flood risk or drainage concerns on or immediately adjacent to this land?
questions.why: Many Lagos parcels are in flood-prone areas that are not disclosed in title documents.

questions.q: Are the boundary beacons in place, undisturbed, and consistent with the survey plan?
questions.why: Missing or moved beacons may indicate a boundary dispute with a neighbouring occupant.

sections.heading: Questions for the Seller
sections.note: These questions should ideally be put in writing, with responses in writing, and reviewed by your lawyer before you rely on them.

questions.q: How did you acquire this property, and can you provide full documentary evidence of your acquisition?
questions.why: Gaps in the acquisition story are a warning sign.

questions.q: Has the property ever been subject to litigation, a government acquisition notice, or a court order?
questions.why: Sellers are legally required to disclose known material defects. Asking in writing protects you.

questions.q: Are there any tenants, occupants, or claimants in possession of or claiming rights over any part of the land?
questions.why: Undisclosed occupants can complicate possession after purchase.

questions.q: Is the property encumbered by any mortgage, charge, or lien?
questions.why: A mortgagee can repossess regardless of your purchase.

questions.q: Are you the sole owner, or are there co-owners, family members, or other parties whose consent is required?
questions.why: A partial owner selling the whole parcel without co-owners' consent is a frequent cause of dispute.
